answer: In node2vec (Grover & Leskovec, 2016), the Wikipedia dataset is a word co-occurrence network built from the first million bytes of English Wikipedia. Nodes are words, and an edge links two words that appear near each other in the text. Node labels are part-of-speech (POS) tags assigned by the Stanford POS-Tagger, so the task is multi-label classification of each word's syntactic role. node2vec learns feature embeddings from biased random walks over this graph and feeds them to a one-vs-rest logistic regression classifier, evaluated across training fractions. The dataset is sparse for cooccurrence edges because an edge exists only when two words actually appear within the context window, so most of the possible word pairs never connect. Many words are rare or occur in few contexts, and the resulting graph has low average degree and weak local structure.
